findings.title: Integer bounds and row bounds of magnitude >= 2^50 are widened by 1 to 4 units; CP-SAT returns .optimal at a point that violates them
findings.claim: README §2.5 (CPSAT row) and §4 'Limits by design': CP-SAT accepts bounds and scaled coefficients below 2^53 and rejects only magnitudes of 2^53 or more; CPModel.swift header: 'CP-SAT works on pure integer programs in exact Int64 arithmetic', 'Root domains, rounded inward to integers'.
findings.observed: With default CPSAT(): x integer in [2^52+1, 2^52+10], min x -> .optimal x = 4503599627370493 (= 2^52-3), CompiledLP.maxViolation bounds = 4.0. x in [2^50+3, 2^50+8] -> .optimal x = 2^50+2 (violation 1.0). x - y = 2^52+1, x in [0,2^52+3], y in [0,10], min x -> .optimal (2^52-3, 0), row violation 4.0. x in [0, 2^53-5], max x -> .optimal 2^53-1 (violation 4.0). With CPSAT(deterministic: true): max x s.t. row x <= 2^50+5 -> .optimal x = 2^50+6. 127x - 125y >= 1 over [-2^52, 2^52] -> y = -(2^52+4).
findings.whyWrong: The bounds are exact integers, exactly representable in Double and inside the accepted range; the returned point is infeasible in exact arithmetic (and by the package's own maxViolation), yet labelled .optimal. CPSAT.violation's relative 1e-6 safety net cannot see a violation of 4 at 4.5e15.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/CPModel.swift:117-119 (snapTolerance = max(1e-9, 4*ulp)) applied as (xl - tol).rounded(.up) / (xu + tol).rounded(.down) at CPModel.swift:173-174 and to row bounds at CPModel.swift:335 and :347; same at LPRelaxation.swift:95 and :99. For |v| >= 2^50, 4 ulp >= 1, so an integral bound moves outward by floor(4 ulp) = 1, 2 or 4.

findings.title: Coefficients that no power of 10 up to 1e6 makes integral (or whose scaling passes 2^53) are silently rounded instead of rejected: false optimum, or SolverError.internalInconsistency
findings.claim: README §2.5 CPSAT row: 'Throws .unsupported for ... data that no power of 10 up to 1e6 makes integral, bounds or scaled coefficients of magnitude 2^53 or more'; §4 Limits: data must become integral when multiplied by a power of 10 up to 10^6. SolverError.internalInconsistency doc (Status.swift): 'A bug in the solver; never caused by user data.'
findings.observed: (2^49+0.375)x + (2^49+0.375)y - (2^50+0.75)z = 0 over binaries, max x+y+z -> CPSAT() .optimal 0 at (0,0,0), although (1,1,1) satisfies the row exactly (CompiledLP.maxViolation 0) with objective 3. 1e-10 x0 + 1e-10 x1 >= 1e-10, min x0+x1 -> .optimal 0 (coefficients zeroed; true 1). max (2^49+0.5)x -> objective 562949953421313 (cost rounded). x - 1.0000000009 y >= 0 with y = 1e6, and (2^48+0.1875)x - 2^48 y <= 0 -> SolverError.internalInconsistency('CP-SAT returned a point that violates row c1') instead of .unsupported. By contrast 1e-7 and 1.0000001 are rejected correctly.
findings.whyWrong: The README promises rejection for this data. 0.375 at 2^49 needs scale 1000 (5.6e17 >= 2^53), 1e-10 and 1.0000000009 need 10^10; instead they are accepted at scale 1 and rounded, which changes the feasible set (false optimum 0 vs 3, labelled .optimal) or trips the final violation check, so valid input gets an error documented as never caused by user data.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/CPModel.swift:122-139 integralScale: a value counts as integral when within snapTolerance = max(1e-9, 4 ulp) (CPModel.swift:117-119), so fractions <= 1e-9, or <= 4 ulp (0.25 at 2^48, 0.5 at 2^49), pass at scale 1; CPModel.swift:302 (rows) and :366 (objective) then round them. CPSAT.swift:286-290 turns the resulting violation into internalInconsistency.

findings.title: With decimal costs and |objective| < 1, CP-SAT stops up to 1e-4 (absolute) from the bound and reports .optimal: answers 2% to 50x off, where its API doc promises an exact proof
findings.claim: CPSAT doc comment (CPSAT.swift:85-88): 'The search stops as soon as the incumbent is within the MIP gap of §6.5 (relative 1e-4, absolute 1e-6) ... this is an exact proof whenever 1e-4·|objective| is smaller than that step'. README risk 10: inexactness is 'Medium on large objective values', 'for CP-SAT, keep objective values below 10^4'. SolutionAnalysis.bound (Analysis.swift:22): 'equals objectiveValue when optimal'.
findings.observed: max 1e-6*x, x integer in [0,50] (one column, no row) -> .optimal objective 1e-06, bound 5e-05 (true 5e-05), with CPSAT() and CPSAT(deterministic: true). min sum_{j=1..50} j*1e-6 x_j s.t. sum x_j >= 1 -> .optimal 5e-05 (the worst feasible choice), bound 0, true 1e-06, in every configuration including CPSAT(). 1e-6-scaled knapsack -> .optimal 1.3e-05 (deterministic, no LP) and 2.3e-05 (4 workers) vs 2.4e-05. Exhaustive enumeration with costs scaled by 10^-ec (ec <= 6): 109 of 2800 solves .optimal with a non-optimal value (0 of 7000 with integral costs).
findings.whyWrong: Step 1e-6 and |objective| <= 5e-5, so 1e-4·|objective| <= 5e-9 < step: the doc promises an exact proof. The stop rule is diff <= max(1e-6, 1e-4·max(1,|incumbent|)), which is an absolute 1e-4 (100 steps, 100x the 'absolute 1e-6' named) whenever |incumbent| <= 1. Shrinking the objective, the README's mitigation, makes it worse. .optimal with bound != objectiveValue also contradicts the SolutionAnalysis.bound contract.

README risk 10 gives the formula max(1e-6, 1e-4·max(1,|incumbent|)), but it describes the trigger as large objective values (>= 10^4, integral costs), rates the impact 'low to medium' and advises keeping objectives below 10^4. findings.title: Root propagation of two parallel rows over a wide domain runs about 1.7*U bound changes inside one propagate() call: time limit, cancellation and memory budget are ignored and RSS grows past 10 GB
findings.claim: CPSAT doc (CPSAT.swift:72-74): timeLimit and task cancellation end the search with .feasible(stoppedBy:) or .noSolution(stoppedBy:); memoryBudgetBytes bounds the learned clauses (rule L7). CPSearch.swift:10-12: 'the loop calls gate.tick() once per propagation round, and forces a full check ... at every restart and every 10,000 propagations'. README §5: CPSAT cancellation latency worst 4.43 ms.
findings.observed: x - y >= 1 and x - y <= 0, x,y integer in [0, U], CPSAT(deterministic: true), timeLimit 1 s: U=1e7 -> .infeasible after 2e7 propagations, 0.60 s, 1.61 GB RSS; U=1e9 -> still running at 8 s (alarm, exit 142), 6.7 GB RSS. 652x - 552y = -1505 over [0,1e9]^2 (infeasible by parity), timeLimit 2 s: CPSAT(), CPSAT(deterministic: true) and CPSAT(lpPropagator: false, deterministic: true) are all still running at 40 s (exit 142), max RSS 12.7 / 10.7 / 7.2 GB. memoryBudgetBytes = 100 MB: still running at 15 s, 10.2 GB. Cancel after 0.5 s (deterministic): no return within 3.5 s (7.3 GB). With the default 8 workers the cooperative pool is saturated, so even the cancelling task does not run.
findings.whyWrong: The model is valid and accepted (bounds < 2^53, tiny activities). A time limit, a cancellation and the memory budget must end any solve; here none is checked until the fixed point, which takes ~1.7*U steps at ~150 bytes each (U=1e9: about 1.7e9 steps).
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCPSAT/CPWorker.swift:651-663: propagate() loops while true to a fixed point with no gate tick, propagation count or memory check. Each pass of propagateLinear (CPWorker.swift:785-807) tightens a bound by slack/a, about 1 unit, interning a new bound literal and trail entry. The only checks are in the search loop: gate.tick() once per propagate() call at CPSearch.swift:106, and the full check every 10,000 propagations between calls. A row whose rounded sides cross (CPModel.swift:326-352 adds each side separately) is not detected at load.

summary: Cycle B, area F5 (CP-SAT), oracles first. The CDCL core held on every check: all 1000 uf50 instances SAT with verified models, all 1000 uuf50 UNSAT, 700 random 3-SAT formulas cross-checked with an independent DPLL, 7280 exhaustive-enumeration solves with integral costs, a Diophantine oracle on wide domains, invariance checks, determinism, portfolio, time limit and cancellation on ordinary hard models, and the seven MIPLIB 3 pure-integer optima with the default configuration. Six findings. Two are critical wrong answers, both from CPModel's snap tolerance max(1e-9, 4 ulp). B5-01: exact integer bounds and right-hand sides of magnitude >= 2^50, inside the documented range, are widened by 1-4, so .optimal comes back at an infeasible point (x = 2^52-3 for x >= 2^52+1). B5-02: data the README says is rejected is silently rounded instead, giving a false optimum (0 vs 3 on an exactly feasible point) or SolverError.internalInconsistency. Both need magnitudes >= 2^48..2^50, or coefficients <= 1e-9 off an integer. B5-03 (high): with decimal costs and |objective| < 1, the fixed gap becomes an absolute 1e-4, so .optimal answers are up to 50x off (a one-column model returns 1e-06 with bound 5e-05), exactly where the CPSAT API doc promises an exact proof. README risk 10 has the formula but misstates the trigger and the mitigation. B5-04 (high): two parallel rows over a wide domain (x-y>=1, x-y<=0 on [0,1e9]) make one propagate() call run ~1.7e9 steps without a gate tick, ignoring the time limit, cancellation and the memory budget while RSS passes 10 GB. B5-05 and B5-06 are low: the 2^53 threshold is off by 4, and the SAT tests skip instead of reporting a known issue. Probe sources: verification/probes/cycle-B/Slots/F5/{main,Oracles,Probes}.swift; log: verification/cycle-B/F5-cpsat.md.
